title: Model vs observation

intro.general: This page puts air temperature from computer models next to temperature that was measured, at the same place. Each line shows how far a month is from its usual value for that calendar month ({{start}} to {{end}}).
intro.expert: Near-surface air temperature from models and reanalyses, next to observations of the same quantity at the same place. Both series are anomalies over their common months ({{start}} to {{end}}): each value minus that series' own mean of the same calendar month, so baselines and units do not matter.

verdict.general: A gap between a model and a measurement does not tell you which one is right. A station measures one point; a model value covers a whole grid cell.
verdict.expert: A difference between a model and an observation does not by itself say which is right. A station is a point and a model value is a grid cell; GISTEMP is a 2° gridded analysis of station and ship observations.

tableNote.general: Trends are in °C per decade. Select a place to draw its chart.
tableNote.expert: Trends in °C per decade over the common months. Select a location to plot the pair.

chart.aria: Anomalies of {{model}} and {{obs}} at {{place}}, and their difference

baseline.general: Zero is each line's own usual value for that calendar month.
baseline.expert: Each series is relative to its own mean of the same calendar month over the common months.

stats.largestStepValue: {{step}} °C at {{month}} (mean of the 6 months from that month minus the 6 months before)
stats.gapChanging: The gap between the two changes by about {{slope}} °C per decade, and that change holds up in the statistical test.
stats.gapUnclear: This record shows no clear change in the gap between the two. That is not the same as no change.
stats.tooFew: Too few common months ({{count}}) for statistics.
